thesis_points: First publicly traded land banking REIT — 876 communities, 139,000 homesites, $8.4B homesite inventory under option
Walkaway risk overplayed: cross-termination pools (97% of invested capital) → max 10% loss per walkaway (5% deposit + 5% fee); 0 walkaways to date
Other Agreements segment growing 3.4x from Q1–Q3 2025 — rapidly diversifying beyond Lennar's ~80% revenue share
IROIC (9.5–10.3%) exceeds WACC; value-accretive at current P/BV of ~0.87x; book value grows as inventory expands
HOPP'R technology platform (centralized land analytics + deal execution) creates a moat difficult to replicate at scale
Consensus analyst: 'Land is land — unless there's a recession, no reason to trade at a discount to book'

key_debate.street: Lennar concentration risk (80% revenue); limited operating history makes walkaway risk difficult to price; housing macro headwinds
key_debate.our_view: Cross-termination pools structurally deter walkaways; Other Agreements rapidly scaling; IROIC > WACC at 1.0x book means equity issuance is accretive

key_dates.note: Watch: SNO pipeline conversion, Forever 21 re-leasing progress
Term loan refinancing — watch spread vs SOFR

thesis_points: Quality over speed: replacing Forever 21 vacancies (~570K sqft) with experiential anchors at >2x legacy rents
New CEO Jackson Hsieh (ex-Spirit Realty) reduced ND/EBITDA from 10.8x → 7.8x within ~1 year of taking office
Crabtree acquisition: fortress-quality asset at $219/SF vs $261/SF peer, 11% going-in cap rate vs ~7-8% peers
Portfolio moat: 42 Class A malls in prime coastal metros (CA, NY, AZ, NJ, PA), $894/SF go-forward tenant sales
16 consecutive quarters of positive leasing spreads; SNO pipeline $90–140M+; new leases 9% above renewals
Deleveraging roadmap: $6.6B → ~$4.5B debt by 2029–2030, targeting ~6x ND/EBITDA via asset sales

key_debate.street: High leverage (8.2x vs SPG 5.7x, SKT 5.4x), tenant bankruptcies (Forever 21, Claire's) signal structural decline
key_debate.our_view: Occupancy gap is deliberate — quality tenants commanding >2x prior rents. Deleveraging credibly underway with $395M B/C sales in 2025

overview.narrative:
REITs posted mixed results Monday with hospitality leading at +0.95% on average, buoyed by strong summer travel demand, while towers (-0.50%) and net lease (-0.46%) lagged as duration-sensitive names faced pressure from a modest backup in the long end. Industrial delivered a solid +0.61% average, though the headline story was REXR's +7.59% surge, likely on earnings or leasing catalysts. Office remained under pressure at -0.43%, with HPP's -4.88% decline dragging the subsector.

The standout divergences deserve attention. ELME's +8.72% move — the day's biggest gainer across all subsectors — suggests a company-specific catalyst, potentially an activist development or strategic review, given housing as a sector was otherwise flat at +0.10%. Similarly, the 960bps spread between REXR and ILPT (-2.07%) within industrials underscores the quality bifurcation still defining that space. In office, the FSP (+2.53%) versus HPP (-4.88%) gap of over 740bps highlights how coastal gateway exposure continues to punish relative to smaller-market portfolios.

Looking ahead, the hospitality and industrial momentum argues for maintaining overweight positioning in those subsectors, but we'd be cautious chasing single-name moves like ELME and REXR without confirming the catalysts. Net lease weakness near -0.46% could present entry points if rate fears prove overdone. Watch for follow-through in towers — CCI at -1.03% looks increasingly stretched.
